text: En la UE, ¿puedo pedirle a una empresa que borre los datos personales que tiene sobre mí?

quotes: los datos personales ya no sean necesarios en relación con los fines
los datos personales hayan sido tratados ilícitamente

expected_answer: Sí: tiene derecho a la supresión sin dilación indebida cuando concurra alguna de las circunstancias del artículo 17.1 (los datos ya no son necesarios para sus fines, retira el consentimiento, se opone al tratamiento, los datos se trataron ilícitamente, deben suprimirse por una obligación legal, o se obtuvieron en relación con servicios de la sociedad de la información del artículo 8.1). Si el responsable hizo públicos los datos, debe adoptar medidas razonables para informar a otros responsables que los traten (17.2). El derecho no es absoluto: no se aplica cuando el tratamiento sea necesario para la libertad de expresión e información, una obligación legal o una misión de interés público, la salud pública, el archivo, la investigación o la estadística, o la defensa de reclamaciones (17.3).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: not an absolute right (17(3)); 'borrar' = supresión; the UK GDPR has a parallel Article 17, so the EU cue is in the question to avoid a jurisdiction miss; the controller, not any company, is the obligor.

text: Under EU rules, what information must a company include when it reports a data breach to the regulator?

quotes: describe the likely consequences of the personal data breach
name and contact details of the data protection officer

expected_answer: The notification must at least describe the nature of the breach (including, where possible, the categories and approximate number of data subjects and of personal data records concerned), give the name and contact details of the data protection officer or another contact point, describe the likely consequences of the breach, and describe the measures taken or proposed to address it, including to mitigate its possible adverse effects (Article 33(3)). If not all of this can be provided at the same time, it may be provided in phases without undue further delay (33(4)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: 'at least' means the list is a minimum; the duty lies on the controller (a processor notifies the controller, 33(2)); the UK GDPR has a parallel Article 33, hence the EU cue.

text: En la UE, ¿en qué casos debe una empresa analizar los riesgos para las personas antes de empezar a tratar sus datos?

quotes: alto riesgo para los derechos y libertades
observación sistemática a gran escala de una zona de acceso público

expected_answer: Cuando un tipo de tratamiento, en particular si utiliza nuevas tecnologías, entrañe probablemente un alto riesgo para los derechos y libertades de las personas físicas, el responsable debe hacer antes una evaluación de impacto relativa a la protección de datos (artículo 35.1). Se requiere en particular en caso de evaluación sistemática y exhaustiva de aspectos personales basada en tratamiento automatizado, como la elaboración de perfiles, con decisiones que produzcan efectos jurídicos o afecten significativamente; de tratamiento a gran escala de categorías especiales de datos o de datos penales; y de observación sistemática a gran escala de una zona de acceso pública (35.3). Además, la autoridad de control publica una lista de operaciones sujetas a evaluación de impacto (35.4) y puede publicar otra de las que no la requieren (35.5).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the list in 35(3) is not exhaustive ('en particular'); national supervisory-authority lists under 35(4)-(5) (not in the corpus) decide many real cases, so a full answer must point to them.

text: Do I need to name a person responsible for data protection in my business in the EU?

quotes: regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale
where required by Union or Member State law shall, designate a data protection officer
Los colegios profesionales y sus consejos generales

expected_answer: Under the GDPR it is mandatory in three cases (Article 37(1)): the processing is carried out by a public authority or body (except courts acting in their judicial capacity); the core activities require regular and systematic monitoring of data subjects on a large scale; or the core activities consist of large-scale processing of special categories of data or of data relating to criminal convictions and offences. Article 37 sets no headcount threshold. Outside those cases the controller or processor may appoint one voluntarily or, where Union or Member State law requires it, must (37(4)); Member State law can therefore add cases (Spain's LOPDGDD Article 34 lists further entities). A group of undertakings may appoint a single officer who is easily accessible from each establishment (37(2)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: my first draft said 'only in three cases', which was wrong: Article 37(4) lets Member State law require more. The answer depends on the Member State, so the Spanish list is an acceptable extra. The original OJ text of 37(1)(c) differs from the consolidated one ('and' vs 'or'): version fixed to the consolidated text.

text: En la UE, ¿puedo llevarme mis datos de un servicio a otro cuando cambio de proveedor?

quotes: en un formato estructurado, de uso común y lectura mecánica
el tratamiento se efectúe por medios automatizados

expected_answer: Sí, en ciertos casos: tiene derecho a recibir los datos personales que haya facilitado a un responsable en un formato estructurado, de uso común y lectura mecánica, y a transmitirlos a otro responsable sin que se lo impida el primero, cuando el tratamiento se base en el consentimiento o en un contrato y se efectúe por medios automatizados (artículo 20.1). También puede pedir que se transmitan directamente de un responsable a otro cuando sea técnicamente posible (20.2). El derecho no se aplica al tratamiento necesario para una misión de interés público o el ejercicio de poderes públicos (20.3) y no debe afectar negativamente a los derechos y libertades de otros (20.4).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: limited to data the person 'provided', to consent- or contract-based processing and to automated means; the limits in 20(3)-(4) were missing from the first draft. Spain adds a social-network portability rule (LOPDGDD Art 95) that applies only to those services.

text: Under EU law, if a company mishandled my data and it harmed me, can I claim compensation, and from whom?

quotes: material or non-material damage
not in any way responsible for the event giving rise to the damage

expected_answer: Yes. Any person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of the GDPR has the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor (Article 82(1)). A controller involved in the processing is liable for damage caused by processing that infringes the Regulation; a processor only where it has not complied with obligations directed specifically to processors or has acted outside or contrary to the controller's lawful instructions (82(2)). Either is exempt if it proves it is not in any way responsible for the event giving rise to the damage (82(3)). Where several controllers or processors are involved and responsible, each is liable for the entire damage so that the data subject is effectively compensated, and one that paid in full can claim back the others' share (82(4)-(5)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the right requires an infringement of the Regulation plus damage; amounts and procedure are left to national courts (not in the corpus). UK GDPR Article 82 is a parallel text, hence the EU cue.

text: En la UE, ¿qué debe decir el contrato entre una empresa y el proveedor que maneja datos personales por su cuenta?

quotes: únicamente siguiendo instrucciones documentadas del responsable
suprimirá o devolverá todos los datos personales una vez finalice la prestación de los servicios de tratamiento
shall immediately inform the controller

expected_answer: Debe ser un contrato u otro acto jurídico vinculante, por escrito (también en formato electrónico), que fije el objeto, la duración, la naturaleza y la finalidad del tratamiento, el tipo de datos y las categorías de interesados, y que establezca que el encargado: trata los datos solo siguiendo instrucciones documentadas del responsable; garantiza la confidencialidad de las personas autorizadas; toma las medidas de seguridad del artículo 32; respeta las condiciones para recurrir a otro encargado; asiste al responsable con los derechos de los interesados y con las obligaciones de los artículos 32 a 36; suprime o devuelve los datos al terminar el servicio; y pone a disposición la información necesaria para demostrar el cumplimiento y permitir auditorías (artículo 28.3 y 28.9). Debe además informar inmediatamente al responsable si, en su opinión, una instrucción infringe la normativa de protección de datos.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the closing sentence of 28(3) (duty to flag an unlawful instruction) and the writing requirement in 28(9) were missing from the first draft; standard contractual clauses (28(7)-(8)) are an alternative route.

text: Under the GDPR, what written records does a business have to keep about how it handles personal data?

quotes: the envisaged time limits for erasure of the different categories of data
employing fewer than 250 persons

expected_answer: Each controller (and its representative) must keep a record of processing activities containing: the name and contact details of the controller and, where applicable, the joint controller, representative and data protection officer; the purposes of the processing; the categories of data subjects and of personal data; the categories of recipients; where applicable, transfers to a third country or international organisation with the documentation of safeguards; where possible, the envisaged time limits for erasure; and, where possible, a general description of the security measures (Article 30(1)). Each processor must keep its own record of the processing it carries out for each controller (30(2)). Records must be in writing, including electronically (30(3)) and be made available to the supervisory authority on request (30(4)). An organisation with fewer than 250 employees is exempt unless its processing is likely to risk data subjects' rights and freedoms, is not occasional, or includes special categories of data (30(5)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: processors have a separate record duty (30(2)); the 250-employee exemption is narrow because 'not occasional' processing, which most businesses do, removes it.

text: En la UE, ¿puede una empresa o una administración usar IA para puntuar a las personas por su comportamiento y tratarlas peor por ello?

quotes: un trato perjudicial o desfavorable hacia determinadas personas físicas o colectivos de personas
Chapters I and II shall apply from 2 February 2025

expected_answer: No: el Reglamento prohíbe introducir en el mercado, poner en servicio o utilizar sistemas de IA para evaluar o clasificar a personas físicas o colectivos durante un período de tiempo atendiendo a su comportamiento social o a características personales conocidas, inferidas o predichas, cuando la puntuación resultante provoque un trato perjudicial o desfavorable en contextos sociales no relacionados con aquellos en que se generaron los datos, o un trato injustificado o desproporcionado con respecto a su comportamiento o su gravedad (artículo 5.1.c). La prohibición se aplica desde el 2 de febrero de 2025 (artículo 113, letra a).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the ban bites only where the score leads to the detrimental treatment described in (i) or (ii); lawful scoring such as credit scoring is not banned as such but is a high-risk use (Annex III point 5(b)). The wording covers public and private actors.

text: What must the person overseeing an AI system used to screen job applicants be able to do?

quotes: disregard, override or reverse the output of the high-risk AI system
automation bias
recruitment or selection of natural persons
2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III

expected_answer: A system used for recruitment or selection is high-risk under Annex III point 4(a), so Article 14 applies: the people assigned human oversight must be enabled, as appropriate and proportionate, to properly understand the system's capacities and limitations and monitor its operation (including anomalies); to remain aware of the tendency to rely automatically on its output (automation bias); to correctly interpret its output; to decide in any situation not to use it or to disregard, override or reverse its output; and to intervene or interrupt it through a stop button or similar procedure that brings it to a halt in a safe state (Article 14(4)). Under the amended Article 113 these requirements apply to Annex III systems from 2 December 2027.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: 'risky decisions' in my first draft was not the legal test; the legal category is 'high-risk' (Article 6, Annex III). The duty to enable oversight is placed on how the provider designs and supplies the system; the application date was postponed by the Omnibus, so an answer that omits it is incomplete today.

text: If I build a customer-service chatbot, do I have to tell people it is an AI?

quotes: informed that they are interacting with an AI system
It shall apply from 2 August 2026

expected_answer: Yes, as a provider you must ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with people are designed and developed so that the people concerned are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless this is obvious to a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect person given the circumstances and context of use (Article 50(1)). Chapter IV is not among the exceptions listed in Article 113, so Article 50(1) applies from the general date of 2 August 2026.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the duty is the provider's (the builder); a business that merely uses a chatbot has deployer duties in 50(3)-(4) for other uses. The obligation is lifted where AI use is obvious, and for some law-enforcement systems.

text: En la UE, ¿tiene mi empresa que formar a sus empleados en el uso de la inteligencia artificial?

quotes: alfabetización en materia de IA de su personal

expected_answer: Según el texto vigente (consolidado a 27 de julio de 2026), los proveedores y los responsables del despliegue de sistemas de IA deben adoptar medidas para apoyar la promoción de la alfabetización en materia de IA de su personal y de otras personas que se encarguen en su nombre del funcionamiento y la utilización de los sistemas, teniendo en cuenta sus conocimientos técnicos, experiencia, educación y formación y el contexto de uso (artículo 4.1). La Comisión y los Estados miembros apoyarán esos esfuerzos, en particular de las pymes (4.2). No se exige garantizar un nivel concreto de alfabetización a ninguna persona.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: Article 4 was rewritten by the Omnibus. The original text required measures 'to ensure, to the best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy' (stricter). The gold is fixed to the consolidated version; a chunk of the original wording would give a wrong answer for today. Applies to those who provide or deploy AI systems, not to every business.

text: What does the AI Act require from a business that uses, rather than builds, a high-risk AI system?

quotes: of at least six months
the affected workers that they will be subject to the use of the high-risk AI system
shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights
2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III

expected_answer: As deployer it must use the system according to its instructions for use with appropriate technical and organisational measures (Article 26(1)); assign human oversight to people with the necessary competence, training, authority and support (26(2)); where it controls the input data, ensure it is relevant and sufficiently representative (26(4)); monitor the system's operation and inform providers where relevant (26(5)); keep the automatically generated logs under its control for at least six months unless other law provides otherwise (26(6)); if an employer, inform workers' representatives and the affected workers before using it at the workplace (26(7)); and, for Annex III systems that make or assist decisions about people, inform those people that they are subject to its use (26(11)). Some deployers (public bodies, providers of public services, and users of certain credit and insurance systems) must also perform a fundamental rights impact assessment (Article 27). These obligations apply to Annex III systems from 2 December 2027 and to Annex I systems from 2 August 2028 (Article 113(c)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the application dates were postponed by the Omnibus, so today these duties are not yet applicable; the list is not exhaustive (26(8)-(10), (12) cover registration, biometric identification and cooperation); the deployer becomes a provider in some cases (Article 25).

text: What kind of information about a person is protected by EU data protection law?

quotes: location data, an online identifier
should be considered to be information on an identifiable natural person
internet protocol addresses, cookie identifiers

expected_answer: Personal data: any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person (the data subject). An identifiable person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data or an online identifier, or to factors specific to their physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural or social identity (Article 4(1)). Online identifiers such as IP addresses and cookie identifiers can leave traces that identify people (recital 30), and pseudonymised data that could be attributed to a person with additional information remains personal data (recital 26).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the definition is broad and context-dependent (recital 26 'means reasonably likely to be used'); truly anonymous information is outside the Regulation.

text: ¿Qué es seudonimizar datos según la normativa europea?

quotes: ya no puedan atribuirse a un interesado sin utilizar información adicional
deben considerarse información sobre una persona física identificable

expected_answer: Es tratar los datos personales de manera que ya no puedan atribuirse a un interesado concreto sin utilizar información adicional, siempre que esa información adicional figure por separado y esté sujeta a medidas técnicas y organizativas que garanticen que los datos no se atribuyan a una persona física identificada o identificable (artículo 4.5). Los datos seudonimizados siguen siendo datos personales cuando podrían atribuirse a una persona mediante información adicional (considerando 26).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: pseudonymisation is a safeguard, not anonymisation; the data stay personal data.

text: Under the GDPR, what does a data breach actually mean in legal terms?

quotes: accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data

expected_answer: A personal data breach is a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data transmitted, stored or otherwise processed (Article 4(12)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: it covers accidental events and internal ones, not only hacking; availability and integrity incidents count as well as confidentiality ones.

text: ¿Cuenta como inteligencia artificial cualquier programa informático, o solo algunos tipos de software según la ley europea?

quotes: infiere de la información de entrada que recibe la manera de generar resultados de salida
los distinguen de los sistemas de software o los planteamientos de programación tradicionales y más sencillos
no debe incluir los sistemas basados en las normas definidas únicamente por personas físicas para ejecutar automáticamente operaciones

expected_answer: No: solo los programas que cumplan la definición de «sistema de IA» (artículo 3, punto 1): un sistema basado en una máquina, diseñado para funcionar con distintos niveles de autonomía, que puede mostrar capacidad de adaptación tras el despliegue y que, para objetivos explícitos o implícitos, infiere de la información de entrada que recibe la manera de generar resultados de salida, como predicciones, contenidos, recomendaciones o decisiones, que pueden influir en entornos físicos o virtuales. El considerando 12 aclara que la definición debe distinguir la IA de los sistemas de software o planteamientos de programación tradicionales y más sencillos y no incluir los sistemas basados en las normas definidas únicamente por personas físicas para ejecutar automáticamente operaciones; la capacidad de inferencia trasciende el tratamiento básico de datos.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER (rewritten after Kevin's comment): the question now asks whether ANY software counts. Ambiguity: where simple statistical or rules-based tools fall is interpretive and turns on the Commission's guidelines on the definition, which are not in the corpus; the answer must stay with Article 3(1) and recital 12 and say the line is not mechanical.

text: What is the difference between building an AI system and just using one, under the AI Act?

quotes: using an AI system under its authority except where the AI system is used in the course of a personal non-professional activity
places it on the market or puts the AI system into service under its own name or trademark
they put their name or trademark on a high-risk AI system already placed on the market

expected_answer: The builder is the provider: it develops an AI system or general-purpose AI model, or has one developed, and places it on the market or puts it into service under its own name or trademark, for payment or free of charge (Article 3(3)). The user is the deployer: a person, public authority or other body using an AI system under its authority, except where it is used in a personal non-professional activity (Article 3(4)). The line can move: a deployer is treated as the provider of a high-risk system if it puts its name or trademark on it, makes a substantial modification, or changes the intended purpose of a system so that it becomes high-risk (Article 25(1)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: 'just using' is the deployer role only while the user does not rebrand, substantially modify or repurpose the system (Article 25); purely personal non-professional use is outside the deployer definition.

text: ¿Qué distingue a un modelo de IA que sirve para muchas tareas distintas de uno hecho para una sola?

quotes: es capaz de realizar de manera competente una gran variedad de tareas distintas
models with at least a billion of parameters

expected_answer: Un modelo de IA de uso general presenta un grado considerable de generalidad y es capaz de realizar de manera competente una gran variedad de tareas distintas, independientemente de la manera en que se introduzca en el mercado, y puede integrarse en diversos sistemas o aplicaciones posteriores; incluye modelos entrenados con un gran volumen de datos mediante autosupervisión a gran escala. Quedan fuera los modelos de IA que se utilicen para actividades de investigación, desarrollo o creación de prototipos antes de su introducción en el mercado (artículo 3, punto 63). El considerando 98 indica que un modelo con al menos mil millones de parámetros entrenado con gran cantidad de datos mediante autosupervisión debe considerarse de generalidad significativa.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the threshold in recital 98 is indicative, not a rule; a narrow-purpose model is outside the definition but the boundary is a matter of degree (guidelines not in the corpus); a model is not an AI system on its own (recital 97).

text: How do I find out whether an AI system I want to use counts as high-risk under EU law?

quotes: AI systems referred to in Annex III shall be considered to be high-risk
shall always be considered to be high-risk where the AI system performs profiling of natural persons

expected_answer: There are two routes. Under Article 6(1), an AI system is high-risk if it is a safety component of a product, or is itself a product, covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I, and that product must undergo a third-party conformity assessment. Under Article 6(2), systems of the kinds listed in Annex III (such as employment, essential services, education) are high-risk. An Annex III system is not high-risk if it does not pose a significant risk of harm to health, safety or fundamental rights, for example because it performs only a narrow procedural task, improves the result of a completed human activity, detects decision patterns without replacing human assessment, or performs a preparatory task (Article 6(3)); but it is always high-risk if it profiles natural persons. The high-risk obligations apply from 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) under Article 113(c).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: classification is a two-step test (Annex III use case, then the Article 6(3) derogation), so Annex III alone does not decide; Article 6 was amended by the Omnibus (6(1a)-(1c) added), so the consolidated text is required.

text: ¿Cómo se combinan el artículo 6 y el artículo 9 del RGPD para tratar datos de salud de los clientes?

quotes: Quedan prohibidos el tratamiento de datos personales que revelen
el interesado dio su consentimiento explícito para el tratamiento de dichos datos personales
el interesado dio su consentimiento para el tratamiento de sus datos personales para uno o varios fines específicos

expected_answer: Los datos relativos a la salud son una categoría especial: su tratamiento está prohibido (artículo 9.1) salvo que concurra alguna de las excepciones del artículo 9.2, por ejemplo el consentimiento explícito (9.2.a) o la medicina preventiva o laboral, el diagnóstico o la asistencia sanitaria (9.2.h). Como el artículo 6.1 dispone que todo tratamiento solo es lícito si se cumple al menos una de sus condiciones, además de la excepción del artículo 9.2 se necesita una base de licitud del artículo 6.1 (por ejemplo, el consentimiento de 6.1.a). El Derecho de la Unión o de los Estados miembros puede establecer que la prohibición no pueda levantarse con el consentimiento del interesado (9.2.a).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the text of Article 9 does not itself say that an Article 6 basis is also needed; the requirement follows from Article 6(1) ('only if') applying to all processing, which is the accepted reading; national law may restrict consent (e.g. in Spain, LOPDGDD Art 9).

text: Can a business in the EU send customer data to a supplier in a country outside the EU, and what must it have in place first?

quotes: shall take place only if
ensures an adequate level of protection
appropriate safeguards, and on condition that enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies for data subjects are available
standard data protection clauses adopted by the Commission
the data subject has explicitly consented to the proposed transfer

expected_answer: Only if the conditions of Chapter V are met (Article 44). First, a transfer may take place where the Commission has decided that the third country, territory or sector ensures an adequate level of protection, with no specific authorisation needed (Article 45(1)). Without such a decision, the controller or processor must provide appropriate safeguards and ensure enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies are available (Article 46(1)), for example standard data protection clauses adopted by the Commission (46(2)(c)). Failing both, a transfer may rely only on a specific derogation in Article 49(1), such as the data subject's explicit consent after being informed of the risks, necessity for a contract, important reasons of public interest, legal claims or vital interests; a narrow residual route exists for non-repetitive transfers concerning a limited number of data subjects.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the countries that currently have an adequacy decision are in Commission decisions that are not in the corpus, as is post-Schrems II practice on supplementary measures; the answer must give the mechanisms, not name countries.

text: En la UE, ¿cómo puedo obtener una copia de los datos que una empresa tiene sobre mí y en cuánto tiempo debe dármela?

quotes: The controller shall provide a copy of the personal data undergoing processing
en el plazo de un mes a partir de la recepción de la solicitud
Dicho plazo podrá prorrogarse otros dos meses

expected_answer: Tiene derecho de acceso (artículo 15): a obtener del responsable la confirmación de si trata datos suyos y, en ese caso, acceso a ellos y a información sobre los fines, las categorías de datos, los destinatarios, el plazo de conservación, sus derechos, el derecho a reclamar ante la autoridad de control, el origen de los datos y la existencia de decisiones automatizadas (15.1), además de una copia de los datos (15.3). El responsable debe responder sin dilación indebida y, en cualquier caso, en el plazo de un mes desde la recepción de la solicitud, prorrogable otros dos meses si es necesario por la complejidad o el número de solicitudes, informándole de la prórroga dentro del primer mes (artículo 12.3). Es gratuito, salvo que las solicitudes sean manifiestamente infundadas o excesivas, en cuyo caso puede cobrar una tasa razonable o negarse (12.5); las copias adicionales pueden dar lugar a una tasa razonable (15.3).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the UK GDPR has parallel but different provisions (clock start, reasonable-search limit); the EU cue is therefore in the question. 'A copy' and the list of information in 15(1) are separate entitlements.

text: ¿A partir de qué edad puede un menor en España dar por sí solo su consentimiento para que una app trate sus datos, y cómo encaja con el RGPD?

quotes: únicamente podrá fundarse en su consentimiento cuando sea mayor de catorce años
tenga como mínimo 16 años

expected_answer: La LOPDGDD (artículo 7.1) establece que el tratamiento de datos de un menor de edad solo podrá fundarse en su consentimiento cuando sea mayor de catorce años, salvo los supuestos en que la ley exija la asistencia de los titulares de la patria potestad o tutela para el acto o negocio jurídico en cuyo contexto se recaba el consentimiento. El RGPD (artículo 8.1) fija con carácter general los 16 años para el consentimiento de un niño en relación con servicios de la sociedad de la información ofrecidos directamente a niños, y por debajo de esa edad exige el consentimiento o la autorización del titular de la patria potestad, pero permite a los Estados miembros fijar por ley una edad inferior; España la fija en 14 años.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the LOPDGDD rule applies to consent-based processing generally, whereas Article 8 GDPR is limited to information society services offered directly to a child; the lower limit allowed to Member States is stated in the rest of Article 8(1) (checked against the text).

text: Does the fundamental rights impact assessment under the AI Act replace the data protection impact assessment under the GDPR?

quotes: include cross-references to the relevant sections of that data protection impact assessment
likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons

expected_answer: No. They are two separate assessments. Article 27 AI Act requires certain deployers of high-risk systems (bodies governed by public law, private entities providing public services, and deployers of the Annex III credit and insurance systems in points 5(b) and (c)) to assess the impact on fundamental rights before deploying the system. Article 27(4) says that where any obligation of that assessment is already met through a data protection impact assessment under Article 35 GDPR, the deployer may cross-refer to the relevant sections or include relevant parts of it, so the two can be linked, but the GDPR assessment remains required where processing is likely to result in a high risk to rights and freedoms (Article 35(1)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: nothing in the text makes one assessment a substitute for the other; 27(4) only allows reuse. Scope of Article 27 is narrower than 'any high-risk system' (excludes Annex III point 2 and limits the deployers).

text: Can an AI provider use sensitive personal data, such as health or ethnic origin, to find and fix bias in its system?

quotes: may exceptionally process special categories of personal data
the bias detection and correction cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data
Processing of personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin

expected_answer: Yes, exceptionally and only under conditions. Under Article 4a(1), providers of high-risk AI systems may process special categories of personal data to the extent strictly necessary for bias detection and correction, subject to appropriate safeguards and in addition to the GDPR, provided that: the bias detection and correction cannot be effectively done with other data, including synthetic or anonymised data; the data are subject to technical limits on re-use and state-of-the-art security and privacy-preserving measures such as pseudonymisation; access is strictly controlled and documented; the data are not transmitted or accessed by other parties; they are deleted once the bias is corrected or the retention period ends; and the records of processing explain why the processing was strictly necessary. Under 4a(2), providers and deployers of other AI systems and models, and deployers of high-risk systems, may do the same where strictly necessary to address biases likely to affect health and safety, fundamental rights or lead to prohibited discrimination, with all the conditions applied; there is no obligation to carry out bias detection.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: this rule exists only in the consolidated text (it replaced Article 10(5) of the original, see q046); the date from which Article 4a applies is not stated in the text read and is not asserted.

text: En la UE, ¿está prohibida la IA que manipula a las personas sin que lo noten, y qué pasa si una empresa la usa?

quotes: deploys subliminal techniques beyond a person’s consciousness
El no respeto de la prohibición de las prácticas de IA a que se refiere el artículo 5 estará sujeto a multas administrativas
whichever thereof is lower

expected_answer: Sí. El artículo 5.1.a prohíbe introducir en el mercado, poner en servicio o utilizar un sistema de IA que despliegue técnicas subliminales que trasciendan la conciencia de una persona, o técnicas deliberadamente manipuladoras o engañosas, con el objetivo o el efecto de alterar de manera sustancial su comportamiento al reducir apreciablemente su capacidad de tomar una decisión informada, de forma que tome una decisión que no habría tomado de otro modo y que cause o sea razonablemente probable que cause un perjuicio considerable. El incumplimiento está sujeto a multas administrativas de hasta 35 000 000 EUR o, si el infractor es una empresa, de hasta el 7 % de su volumen de negocios mundial total del ejercicio anterior, si esta cuantía fuese superior (artículo 99.3); en el caso de las pymes, incluidas las empresas emergentes, se aplica la cuantía o el porcentaje que sea menor (99.6).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the prohibition requires a distorting objective or effect and a significant harm; Member States set the penalty rules but Article 99(3) fixes the ceiling; the SME rule is 'whichever is lower'.

text: If an automated system makes an important decision about me, like refusing a loan, how do the EU and UK rules differ on my right to challenge it?

quotes: The data subject shall have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing
there is no meaningful human involvement in the taking of the decision
may not be taken based solely on automated processing, unless one of the following conditions is met
enable the data subject to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller

expected_answer: EU: Article 22(1) gives the data subject the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them; Article 22(2) excepts decisions necessary for a contract, authorised by law with suitable safeguards, or based on explicit consent, and 22(3) requires at least the right to obtain human intervention, express a point of view and contest the decision in the contract and consent cases. UK: Article 22 is replaced by Articles 22A to 22D. A decision is 'solely automated' if there is no meaningful human involvement (considering the extent of profiling) and 'significant' if it has a legal or similarly significant effect (22A). Significant solely automated decisions based on special category data are restricted unless a condition is met (22B), and for any significant solely automated decision based on personal data the controller must ensure safeguards: information, the ability to make representations, to obtain human intervention and to contest (22C).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: describing the UK regime as 'more permissive' is a characterisation; the answer should stay with what each text provides. UK Article 22 itself survives only as a placeholder in the corpus (see the data-quality note).

text: ¿Cuál es la edad mínima para que un menor consienta por sí solo el uso de sus datos en un servicio online, en la UE y en el Reino Unido?

quotes: tenga como mínimo 16 años
the child is at least 13 years old
The Secretary of State may by regulations make provision about verifying

expected_answer: UE: el RGPD (artículo 8.1) fija 16 años para el consentimiento de un niño en servicios de la sociedad de la información ofrecidos directamente a niños, y permite a los Estados miembros fijar por ley una edad inferior; España la fija en 14 años (LOPDGDD, artículo 7.1). Reino Unido: el artículo 8.1 del UK GDPR fija 13 años; el artículo 8ZA permite al Secretario de Estado regular por reglamento la verificación de la edad.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the EU figure is a default that Member States can lower, so 'the EU age' is not one number; the UK figure is a single rule. Applies only to consent-based processing in information society services offered directly to a child.

text: What is a recognised legitimate interest in UK data protection law, and is there anything like it in the EU GDPR?

quotes: processing is necessary for the purposes of a recognised legitimate interest
responding to an emergency
safeguarding a vulnerable individual
legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party

expected_answer: In the UK GDPR, Article 6(1)(ea) adds, as a lawful basis, processing that is necessary for the purposes of a recognised legitimate interest; the recognised interests are listed in Annex 1 (for example responding to an emergency and safeguarding a vulnerable individual). The EU GDPR has no such list: Article 6(1)(f) allows processing necessary for the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or a third party except where overridden by the interests or fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject, so a balancing test is always needed.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: 'nothing like it' is true of the operative text of Article 6; recitals of the EU GDPR give examples of legitimate interests but create no pre-approved list. The UK basis applies from 5 February 2026 (see q049).

text: ¿Cómo deciden la UE y el Reino Unido si un país tercero es seguro para transferirle datos personales?

quotes: ensures an adequate level of protection
the Secretary of State may by regulations approve transfers of personal data to
not materially lower than the standard of the protection

expected_answer: UE: la Comisión decide que el tercer país, un territorio o sector, o la organización internacional garantiza un nivel de protección adecuado; esa transferencia no requiere autorización específica (artículo 45.1). Al evaluarlo tiene en cuenta, entre otros, el Estado de derecho y los derechos humanos, la legislación, la existencia y funcionamiento de autoridades de control independientes y los compromisos internacionales (45.2). Reino Unido: el Secretario de Estado puede aprobar por reglamento transferencias a un tercer país o una organización internacional (artículo 45A) si se cumple la «prueba de protección de datos»: que el nivel de protección no sea sustancialmente inferior al del Reino Unido (artículo 45B.1), considerando, entre otros, el Estado de derecho y los derechos humanos, la autoridad encargada de velar por la protección de datos, las vías de reparación, las normas sobre transferencias posteriores y las obligaciones internacionales (45B.2).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the EU test is 'adequate level of protection' decided by the Commission; the UK test is 'not materially lower' decided by the Secretary of State; whether these standards differ in practice is not settled by the text. The decisions themselves are not in the corpus.

text: Does UK data protection law treat research and statistics differently from the EU's GDPR?

quotes: Personal data may only be processed for RAS purposes if
scientific research or historical research
shall be subject to appropriate safeguards

expected_answer: Yes in structure. The UK GDPR has its own Chapter (Articles 84A to 84D) for processing for scientific or historical research, archiving in the public interest and statistical purposes ('RAS purposes'). Article 84B allows such processing only if it consists of collecting the data, converts it into information that does not permit identification, or the RAS purposes cannot otherwise be fulfilled, and requires appropriate safeguards; Article 84C says when that safeguards requirement is satisfied and Article 84D lets the Secretary of State make further provision by regulations. The EU GDPR deals with it in Article 89(1): processing for these purposes is subject to appropriate safeguards, with technical and organisational measures in particular to ensure data minimisation.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: 'differently' is about where and how it is regulated; whether outcomes differ in practice is not answerable from the text alone.

text: ¿A qué autoridad puedo reclamar si usan mal mis datos, en la UE y en el Reino Unido?

quotes: right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority
may make a complaint to the Commission

expected_answer: UE: todo interesado tiene derecho a presentar una reclamación ante una autoridad de control, en particular en el Estado miembro de su residencia habitual, lugar de trabajo o lugar de la supuesta infracción (artículo 77.1 RGPD). Reino Unido: el interesado puede presentar una reclamación ante la Comisión si considera que hay una infracción del UK GDPR o de las Partes 3 o 4 de la Ley de Protección de Datos de 2018 (artículo 165.2 de esa Ley), que sustituye al artículo 77 del UK GDPR.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the UK complaint right sits in the DPA 2018 (section 165), not in the UK GDPR, whose Article 77 is omitted; the text calls the body 'the Commission' without naming it further.

text: How does the test for reusing personal data for a new purpose differ between the UK GDPR and the EU GDPR?

quotes: any link between the purposes for which the personal data have been collected
Processing of personal data for a new purpose is to be treated as processing in a manner compatible with the original purpose where

expected_answer: Both ask whether the new purpose is compatible with the original one, weighing the link between the purposes, the context of collection and the relationship with the controller, the nature of the data (including special categories and criminal-offence data), the possible consequences for data subjects and the existence of safeguards (Article 6(4)(a) to (e) EU GDPR; Article 8A(2) UK GDPR). The UK GDPR adds, in Article 8A(3), cases that are treated as compatible: consent to a specified, explicit and legitimate new purpose; research, archiving or statistics under Article 84B; ensuring compliance with Article 5(1); a condition in Annex 2; or safeguarding certain public-interest objectives authorised by law. Where the original basis was consent, only some of these routes apply (Article 8A(4)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the EU text applies the factor test where the new purpose is not based on consent or law; the UK adds listed 'deemed compatible' cases that have no counterpart in Article 6(4).

text: ¿Cuánto tiempo tiene una empresa para responder a mi solicitud de acceso a mis datos, en la UE y en el Reino Unido?

quotes: en el plazo de un mes a partir de la recepción de la solicitud
the latest of the following

expected_answer: UE: sin dilación indebida y, en cualquier caso, en el plazo de un mes desde la recepción de la solicitud, prorrogable otros dos meses si es necesario por la complejidad o el número de solicitudes, con aviso en el primer mes y motivos (artículo 12.3 RGPD). Reino Unido: el «plazo aplicable» es un mes que comienza en el «momento pertinente», que es el último de estos: la recepción de la solicitud, la recepción de la información pedida para confirmar la identidad, o el pago de la tasa si la hay (artículo 12A.1 y 12A.2); puede ampliarse dos meses más mediante aviso, antes de que acabe ese mes y con indicación de los motivos, por la complejidad o el número de solicitudes (12A.3 y 12A.4).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: in the UK the clock can start later than receipt of the request (identity information, fee), which has no counterpart in the EU text.

text: When I ask a UK company for a copy of my data, does it have to search everywhere, as in the EU?

quotes: reasonable and proportionate search
the right to obtain from the controller confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning him or her are being processed

expected_answer: In the UK GDPR, Article 15(1A) says the data subject is only entitled to such confirmation, personal data and other information as the controller can provide based on a reasonable and proportionate search. The EU text of Article 15(1) contains no such wording: it gives the right to obtain confirmation, access to the personal data and the listed information. How far an EU controller must search is therefore not stated in the text.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the absence of express wording in the EU text does not settle the EU position (case law and guidance, not in the corpus, address scope); the answer should say the text is silent, not that the EU requires an unlimited search. The UK limit applies from 30 September 2026 per the corpus metadata.

text: ¿Pueden mis familiares acceder a mis datos personales o pedir que se supriman cuando yo fallezca?

quotes: Las personas vinculadas al fallecido por razones familiares o de hecho así como sus herederos podrán dirigirse al responsable

expected_answer: Sí, con límites. Las personas vinculadas al fallecido por razones familiares o de hecho, así como sus herederos, pueden dirigirse al responsable o encargado para solicitar el acceso a los datos personales y, en su caso, su rectificación o supresión; no pueden hacerlo cuando el fallecido lo hubiese prohibido expresamente o así lo establezca una ley, aunque esa prohibición no afecta al derecho de los herederos a acceder a los datos de carácter patrimonial (artículo 3.1). También pueden actuar las personas o instituciones designadas expresamente por el fallecido (3.2). En caso de fallecimiento de menores, sus representantes legales o el Ministerio Fiscal, y en el de personas con discapacidad, también quienes ejercían funciones de apoyo (3.3).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: this is Spanish law only; the GDPR does not cover deceased persons and leaves the matter to Member States. The prohibition by the deceased does not bar heirs from patrimonial data.

text: Can a shop in Spain film the public street outside its door with a security camera, and what must it do with the recordings?

quotes: Solo podrán captarse imágenes de la vía pública en la medida en que resulte imprescindible
Los datos serán suprimidos en el plazo máximo de un mes desde su captación

expected_answer: Only to the extent that it is essential for the security purpose: images of the public road may be captured only insofar as indispensable (Article 22(2)). A larger area is possible only where needed to secure strategic installations or transport infrastructure, and never the interior of a private home. The recordings must be deleted within a maximum of one month from capture, unless they are needed as evidence of acts against the integrity of persons, property or installations, in which case they must be made available to the competent authority within seventy-two hours of learning of the recording (22(3)). The duty to inform is met by a sufficiently visible information device stating at least that the processing exists, who the controller is and that rights can be exercised, and the controller must keep the full information available (22(4)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: other conditions (a proportionality assessment, sector rules) are outside the article; the limit 'imprescindible' is a necessity test applied case by case.

text: ¿Puede mi jefe exigirme que conteste mensajes del trabajo durante mis vacaciones?

quotes: tendrán derecho a la desconexión digital a fin de garantizar, fuera del tiempo de trabajo legal o convencionalmente establecido, el respeto de su tiempo de descanso, permisos y vacaciones

expected_answer: La ley reconoce a los trabajadores y empleados públicos el derecho a la desconexión digital fuera del tiempo de trabajo legal o convencionalmente establecido, para garantizar el respeto de su tiempo de descanso, permisos y vacaciones y de su intimidad personal y familiar (artículo 88.1). Las modalidades de ejercicio atenderán a la naturaleza y objeto de la relación laboral, favorecerán la conciliación y se sujetarán a lo que establezca la negociación colectiva o, en su defecto, a lo acordado entre la empresa y los representantes de los trabajadores (88.2). El empleador, previa audiencia de los representantes, elaborará una política interna que defina esas modalidades y las acciones de formación (88.3).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the text states a right to digital disconnection but leaves the practical modalities to collective bargaining or an internal policy, so it does not literally say an employer 'cannot ask'; employment-law consequences are outside the corpus.

text: Can my employer in Spain use video cameras to monitor employees at work?

quotes: Los empleadores habrán de informar con carácter previo, y de forma expresa, clara y concisa
En ningún caso se admitirá la instalación de sistemas de grabación de sonidos ni de videovigilancia en lugares destinados al descanso o esparcimiento

expected_answer: Yes, within limits. Employers may process camera images to exercise the control functions provided in Article 20.3 of the Workers' Statute and in public-service legislation, provided those functions are exercised within their legal framework and its inherent limits, and they must inform employees (and, where applicable, their representatives) beforehand, expressly, clearly and concisely (Article 89(1)). Where an employee is caught committing a flagrant unlawful act, the duty to inform is met if at least the information device of Article 22(4) exists. Sound recording and video surveillance are never allowed in places for rest or recreation such as changing rooms, toilets and canteens (89(2)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the Workers' Statute and case law on proportionality are outside the corpus; sound recording and other devices have further rules (Article 89(3), not asserted).

text: ¿Puedo pedir a un buscador que quite de los resultados de mi nombre unas noticias antiguas sobre mí?

quotes: eliminen de las listas de resultados que se obtuvieran tras una búsqueda efectuada a partir de su nombre los enlaces publicados
Este derecho subsistirá aun cuando fuera lícita la conservación de la información publicada en el sitio web

expected_answer: Sí, en ciertos casos. Toda persona tiene derecho a que los motores de búsqueda eliminen de las listas de resultados obtenidas tras una búsqueda a partir de su nombre los enlaces publicados que contengan información relativa a ella cuando sean inadecuados, inexactos, no pertinentes, no actualizados o excesivos, o hayan pasado a serlo por el transcurso del tiempo, teniendo en cuenta los fines para los que se recogieron, el tiempo transcurrido y la naturaleza e interés público de la información (artículo 93.1). Lo mismo si sus circunstancias personales evidencian la prevalencia de sus derechos sobre el mantenimiento de los enlaces, y el derecho subsiste aunque sea lícita la conservación de la información en el sitio web de origen.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the right is to delisting from name searches, not deletion of the source page; the balancing against public interest is built into the text, so old news about a public matter may remain.

text: Can I make a social network in Spain delete the posts and photos I uploaded?

quotes: a que sean suprimidos, a su simple solicitud, los datos personales que hubiese facilitado para su publicación por servicios de redes sociales
Se exceptúan de lo dispuesto en este apartado los datos que hubiesen sido facilitados por personas físicas en el ejercicio de actividades personales o domésticas

expected_answer: Yes. Article 94(1) gives everyone the right to have the personal data they provided for publication on social networks and equivalent information society services erased on simple request. For data that others provided, Article 94(2) gives the right to erasure where the data are inadequate, inaccurate, not pertinent, not up to date or excessive, or became so over time, taking into account the purposes, the time elapsed and the nature and public interest of the information, and also where personal circumstances show that the person's rights prevail; data provided by individuals in purely personal or household activities are excepted.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the 'simple request' right covers what the person themselves provided; for others' posts the balanced test in 94(2) applies and the household exception removes ordinary private posts.

text: En España, ¿cómo se clasifica la infracción de no avisar a la autoridad de una brecha de seguridad de datos?

quotes: El incumplimiento del deber de notificación a la autoridad de protección de datos de una violación de seguridad de los datos personales
La notificación incompleta, tardía o defectuosa a la autoridad de protección de datos

expected_answer: No notificar la violación de seguridad a la autoridad de protección de datos, en el sentido del artículo 33 del RGPD, es una infracción grave (artículo 73.r), que prescribe a los dos años. En cambio, la notificación incompleta, tardía o defectuosa se considera una infracción leve (artículo 74.m), que prescribe al año.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: whether a given notification is 'late' or 'not made' is a question of fact; the classification determines the limitation period (the sanction amounts are in Article 76 and in GDPR Article 83, not asserted here).

text: As of the start of 2026, when were the AI Act's rules for high-risk AI systems due to start applying?

quotes: It shall apply from 2 August 2026
Article 6(1) and the corresponding obligations in this Regulation shall apply from 2 August 2027

expected_answer: Under the Regulation as originally published, it applied generally from 2 August 2026, which was therefore the start date for the high-risk rules for the Annex III systems, while Article 6(1) (the product-safety route through Annex I) and the corresponding obligations applied from 2 August 2027 (Article 113 as originally published). These dates were later changed by the 2026 Omnibus Regulation.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force 27 July 2026) replaced these dates; the original text is the correct source only for a date before that. The gold requires the original (OJ) wording.

text: En 2025, ¿qué exigía exactamente el Reglamento de IA a las empresas sobre la formación de su personal en IA?

quotes: en la mayor medida posible
nivel suficiente de alfabetización en materia de IA

expected_answer: En el texto original, los proveedores y responsables del despliegue de sistemas de IA debían adoptar medidas para garantizar que, en la mayor medida posible, su personal y demás personas que se encargasen en su nombre del funcionamiento y la utilización de sistemas de IA tuvieran un nivel suficiente de alfabetización en materia de IA, teniendo en cuenta sus conocimientos técnicos, experiencia, educación y formación y el contexto de uso (artículo 4 en su redacción original, aplicable desde el 2 de febrero de 2025). El texto actual, tras el Ómnibus de 2026, exige solo adoptar medidas para apoyar la promoción de esa alfabetización.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the original duty was 'ensure, to the best extent, a sufficient level'; the amended one is 'support the promotion'. Pair with q012; the gold requires the OJ wording.

text: Before the 2026 amendments, was it lawful for the makers of an AI tool to use people's sensitive data, such as ethnic origin, to check that their system treated groups fairly?

quotes: the bias detection and correction cannot be effectively fulfilled by processing other data

expected_answer: Yes, exceptionally: Article 10(5) of the original text allowed providers of high-risk AI systems to process special categories of personal data to the extent strictly necessary for bias detection and correction, subject to appropriate safeguards and conditions, including that the bias detection cannot be effectively done with other data (including synthetic or anonymised data), technical limits on re-use, strict access controls, no transfer to other parties, deletion once the bias is corrected or the retention period ends, and records explaining why the processing was strictly necessary. The current consolidated text moves this rule to the new Article 4a and extends it.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: in the consolidated text Article 10(5) no longer exists (verified); the gold requires the OJ wording. Pair with q026.

text: Tras las últimas modificaciones del Reglamento de IA, ¿qué autoridad supervisa los sistemas de IA basados en un modelo de uso general del mismo proveedor, y qué poderes tiene?

quotes: The AI Office shall be exclusively competent for the supervision and enforcement of the obligations under this Regulation
the AI Office shall have all the powers of a market surveillance authority
may be accompanied by the imposition of penalties in accordance with Article 99(3) to (7)

expected_answer: La Oficina de IA es la única competente para supervisar y hacer cumplir las obligaciones del Reglamento respecto de los sistemas de IA basados en modelos de uso general cuando el modelo y el sistema los desarrolla el mismo proveedor (o proveedores de la misma empresa), con excepciones (productos del anexo I, sistemas del anexo III punto 2, determinados sistemas de autoridades policiales, fronteras e instituciones financieras, y administración de justicia), y respecto de los sistemas que constituyan o se integren en una plataforma o motor de búsqueda en línea de muy gran tamaño (artículo 75.1). Tiene todos los poderes de una autoridad de vigilancia del mercado y puede abrir investigaciones, pedir información e inspeccionar (artículo 75 bis), aceptar compromisos vinculantes (75 ter), y adoptar decisiones de incumplimiento que pueden acompañarse de multas conforme al artículo 99.3 a 99.7 y de multas coercitivas periódicas (75 quater).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: Articles 75a to 75d are new in the consolidated text (inserted by the Omnibus) and 75(1) was rewritten; in the original text the Office's role was different, so only the consolidated version answers. The Spanish numbering of inserted articles may read 75 bis to 75 quinquies; the summary here is limited and omits procedural safeguards.

text: In the GDPR as first published in the Official Journal, how was the third trigger for appointing a data protection officer worded, and how does the current consolidated text word it?

quotes: special categories of data pursuant to Article 9 and personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences
special categories of data pursuant to Article 9 or personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences

expected_answer: As first published, Article 37(1)(c) referred to large-scale processing of special categories of data pursuant to Article 9 'and' personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences referred to in Article 10, which read literally could be taken to require both. The current consolidated text says 'or', so either kind of data triggers the duty.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the word difference is the only change in this unit between the two versions (verified). The reason for the change is not stated in the text and is not asserted here.

text: ¿Desde cuándo pueden las organizaciones del Reino Unido basarse en un «interés legítimo reconocido» para tratar datos?

quotes: processing is necessary for the purposes of a recognised legitimate interest

expected_answer: Desde el 5 de febrero de 2026, fecha desde la que se aplica la versión vigente de esta base de licitud (artículo 6.1.ea del UK GDPR, introducida por la Ley de Datos (Uso y Acceso) de 2025).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the date is the corpus metadata in_force_from (2026-02-05), taken from the legislation.gov.uk restriction date; it agrees with the commencement information gathered earlier in the project. The answer needs the date metadata surfaced by the pipeline, since it is not in the provision text.

text: ¿Desde cuándo pueden hacerse por videoconferencia las actuaciones de investigación de la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos?

quotes: Las actuaciones de investigación podrán realizarse a través de sistemas digitales que, mediante la videoconferencia

expected_answer: Desde el 10 de mayo de 2023, fecha de la versión del artículo 53 bis de la LOPDGDD que lo incorpora: permite que las actuaciones de investigación se realicen a través de sistemas digitales de videoconferencia u otro sistema similar que permita la comunicación bidireccional y simultánea de imagen y sonido entre la Agencia y el inspeccionado, garantizando la transmisión y recepción seguras de documentos e información; se utilizan cuando lo determine la Agencia y requieren la conformidad del inspeccionado.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: Article 53 bis did not exist in the 2018 text (verified against the 2018 version); the date is the BOE version date in_force_from (2023-05-10), which here belongs to the article itself because it is a single-version block. For other BOE articles in_force_from is the date of the block's latest version, not of each paragraph, so such dates must not be used paragraph by paragraph.

text: Since when can a person ask a UK company to erase data that was processed because of a malicious person's allegation?

quotes: which was made by a person who is a malicious person in relation to the data subject

expected_answer: From 31 March 2026: Article 17(1)(g) of the UK GDPR gives a right to erasure where the personal data have been processed as a result of an allegation about the data subject that was made by a malicious person, has been investigated by the controller, and in relation to which the controller has decided that no further action is to be taken.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER (legal term of art kept on purpose, so the leakage warning is expected): the date is the corpus metadata in_force_from (2026-03-31), which matches the government's commencement information gathered earlier; the answer needs that metadata. The definition of 'malicious person' is elsewhere in the Act and is not asserted.

text: What is the highest fine a company can get under EU data protection law?

quotes: up to 20 000 000 EUR

expected_answer: Up to EUR 20,000,000 or, for an undertaking, up to 4 % of its total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher, for the infringements listed in Article 83(5) (such as the basic principles for processing, conditions for consent, data subjects' rights and international transfers).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: this is the upper of two tiers (83(4) is EUR 10 million or 2 %); these are ceilings per infringement, and national law governs how they are applied; the UK fines are in pounds (UK GDPR 83 and DPA 2018 s.157).

text: ¿Cómo de grande puede ser la multa por usar una práctica de IA que la UE ha prohibido?

quotes: multas administrativas de hasta 35 000 000 EUR
whichever thereof is lower

expected_answer: Hasta 35 000 000 EUR o, si el infractor es una empresa, hasta el 7 % de su volumen de negocios mundial total correspondiente al ejercicio financiero anterior, si esta cuantía fuese superior (artículo 99.3); para las pymes, incluidas las empresas emergentes, se aplica la menor de ambas cuantías (artículo 99.6).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: ceilings, not fixed amounts; the SME rule inverts 'whichever is higher'.

text: How long does a company have to report a data breach to the authorities under EU rules?

quotes: not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it

expected_answer: Without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after becoming aware of it, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons; if the notification is later than 72 hours it must be accompanied by reasons for the delay (Article 33(1)).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the clock runs from awareness, not occurrence; 'where feasible' and the risk threshold qualify the 72 hours, so it is a default, not an absolute figure.

text: En la UE, ¿cuánto tiempo tiene una empresa para responder cuando le pido ejercer un derecho sobre mis datos?

quotes: en el plazo de un mes a partir de la recepción de la solicitud
Dicho plazo podrá prorrogarse otros dos meses

expected_answer: Sin dilación indebida y, en cualquier caso, en el plazo de un mes a partir de la recepción de la solicitud; ese plazo puede prorrogarse otros dos meses en caso necesario, teniendo en cuenta la complejidad y el número de solicitudes, y el responsable debe informar de la prórroga y de los motivos dentro del primer mes (artículo 12.3).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: applies to requests under Articles 15 to 22; the extension must be notified within the first month.

text: From what date do the AI Act's rules for high-risk AI systems, like those used in hiring, apply?

quotes: 2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III

expected_answer: For AI systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(2) and Annex III (which includes recruitment and selection), from 2 December 2027; for systems classified as high-risk under Article 6(1) and Annex I (products covered by Union harmonisation legislation), from 2 August 2028 (Article 113(c) as amended).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the original dates (2 August 2026 and 2 August 2027) were replaced by the Omnibus, so a figure from the original text is wrong today; Article 6(5) is excepted.

text: En la UE, ¿a qué edad puede un niño aceptar por sí solo que un servicio online use sus datos?

quotes: tenga como mínimo 16 años
siempre que esta no sea inferior a 13 años

expected_answer: A los 16 años con carácter general (artículo 8.1 RGPD, para servicios de la sociedad de la información ofrecidos directamente a niños cuando el tratamiento se basa en el consentimiento); por debajo de esa edad hace falta el consentimiento o la autorización del titular de la patria potestad. Los Estados miembros pueden fijar por ley una edad inferior, que no puede ser inferior a 13 años (España: 14 años).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: 16 is a default that Member States may lower to no less than 13; so the answer depends on the Member State, and for the UK it is 13 (see q029).

text: What rights do California residents have to opt out of the sale of their personal information?
expected_answer: Decline: US state privacy law is outside the corpus, which covers EU, Spanish and UK data-protection and AI law. Offer to explain the equivalent rights under the GDPR or UK GDPR instead.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: no US material is in the corpus (checked by search).

text: ¿Qué dice la ley federal alemana de protección de datos sobre los datos de los empleados?
expected_answer: Rechazar: la legislación nacional alemana no está en el corpus, que solo contiene el RGPD y el Reglamento de IA de la UE, la normativa del Reino Unido y la ley orgánica española. Se puede explicar lo que el RGPD dice sobre el tratamiento en el ámbito laboral (artículo 88) y recordar que cada Estado miembro puede añadir normas.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: GDPR Article 88 lets Member States legislate on employment; the German statute itself is not in the corpus (checked by search).

text: What did the Court of Justice decide in the Schrems II case about sending data to the US?
expected_answer: Decline: case law of the Court of Justice is outside the corpus. Offer to explain what the GDPR text itself says about international transfers (Articles 44 to 49).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: no judgments are in the corpus (Tier 3, not yet ingested); this question will need revisiting if case law is added (gold version 2).

text: ¿Cuál ha sido la mayor multa impuesta nunca por el RGPD y a quién?
expected_answer: Rechazar: las decisiones sancionadoras concretas no están en el corpus. Se puede explicar el límite máximo que fija el artículo 83.5 del RGPD, pero no qué multas se han impuesto.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: enforcement decisions are Tier 3 and not ingested; the ceiling is in the corpus but the fact asked for is not.

text: ¿Qué recomienda la guía de la AEPD sobre análisis de riesgos para una pyme?
expected_answer: Rechazar: las guías de la AEPD no forman parte del corpus (su licencia no permite incluirlas). Se puede explicar lo que dice el RGPD sobre la evaluación de impacto (artículo 35) y la seguridad del tratamiento (artículo 32).
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: the AEPD guides are CC BY-NC-SA and deliberately excluded.

text: Is my company compliant with data protection law?
expected_answer: Decline to give a compliance verdict: that requires the facts of the business and legal advice. Offer to explain what the relevant provisions require, such as lawful basis, records, security and breach notification, so the user can assess their position or consult a lawyer.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: a general compliance verdict cannot be given from the texts; the assistant explains law, it does not apply it to a business.

text: ¿Debería denunciar a mi empresa porque monitoriza mis correos electrónicos?
expected_answer: Rechazar dar un consejo sobre si denunciar: depende de los hechos y requiere asesoramiento jurídico. Se puede explicar qué dicen las normas sobre el control por el empleador (por ejemplo, el artículo 89 de la LOPDGDD sobre videovigilancia laboral, o el deber de información del RGPD) y a qué autoridad se puede reclamar.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: decision to sue or complain is a legal strategy question; the corpus has no rule specific to email monitoring that settles it.

text: Can you write a privacy policy for my online shop?
expected_answer: Decline to draft a binding legal document: that is legal work that depends on the shop's actual processing. Offer to explain what information the GDPR requires to be given to individuals (Articles 13 and 14) so the user can prepare or review a policy.
author: claude
notes: LAWYER: drafting a policy is legal service provision; explaining the information duties is within scope.
